title: AWS: connect an account for the first time
chapter_timing: Receipt-bound logical chapters include control cue, actual transition and confirmation; durations are video times.

steps.title: Goal. Connect an AWS account to CryoLauncher.
instructions: Sign in to CryoStack. In a separate AWS console tab, sign in to the account whose administrator authorized this connection.
You need permission to create the IAM access-role stack through CloudFormation.
Finish this guide at Connected; cloud preparation and model execution are separate later steps.
steps.why: Cloud runs use this account through temporary access to an AWS role.
steps.expected: Start signed in to CryoStack and to an AWS account you are authorized to connect.

steps.title: 1. Choose Cloud in the Mode panel.
instructions: Choose Cloud in the Mode panel.
Scroll to Environment → AWS ACCOUNT.
steps.why: Cloud mode reveals the AWS account connection controls.

steps.title: 2. Under AWS ACCOUNT, choose Connect AWS Account.
instructions: Scroll to Environment and find AWS ACCOUNT. If it says Not connected, choose Connect AWS Account.
Continue when the status says Awaiting role and the setup card appears.
steps.why: CryoStack creates a setup link tied to your signed-in user.
steps.expected: Awaiting role means you can continue to Open AWS Setup.
steps.note: The recording cuts from Cloud selection to the resulting Awaiting role state; the brief off-screen Connect action is explained here.

steps.title: 3. Choose Open AWS Setup.
instructions: Choose Open AWS Setup.
Switch to the AWS tab showing Quick create stack.
steps.why: The button opens the connection-specific CloudFormation setup in a new tab.
steps.expected: Switch to the AWS tab showing Quick create stack.

steps.title: 4. Review the prefilled Quick create stack page.
instructions: Confirm the account in the AWS console before creating resources. Its identity is hidden in this tutorial.
Review the template and its IAM access role. Keep the stack name and connection values generated by CryoStack.
Scroll to the IAM capabilities acknowledgement near the bottom.
steps.why: The generated template links your AWS access role to this CryoStack connection.
steps.expected: Keep the generated stack name and connection parameters; confirm the intended AWS account.
steps.note: Account identifiers, the template query, stack identifiers and connection security values are masked.

steps.title: 5. Review the IAM notice, then check its acknowledgement.
instructions: Read the IAM notice and review what the template creates.
If authorized, check I acknowledge that AWS CloudFormation might create IAM resources.
Keep this acknowledgement checked before choosing Create stack.
Choose Create stack.
AWS starts creating the stack; wait for completion.
Wait for the stack you just created to reach CREATE_COMPLETE.
If the stack fails, inspect its Events before continuing.
The stack name is hidden here; use the stack you created from your own setup link.
steps.why: CloudFormation needs your permission to create the access role. This submits the access-role stack you just reviewed. The role must exist before CryoStack can verify its access.
steps.expected: CREATE_COMPLETE is visible for the created stack.

steps.title: 6. Open the Outputs tab on that stack.
instructions: Open the Outputs tab on that stack.
Find the row whose Key is RoleArn.
In Outputs, locate the row with Key RoleArn.
Select the full text in that row’s Value column and copy it with Ctrl+C on Windows/Linux or Command+C on macOS.
Do not copy the Key label. Do not omit any part of the ARN.
steps.why: Outputs contains the role identifier to return to CryoStack. CryoStack needs the full ARN of the access role created by this stack.
steps.expected: Copy the entire value, not the RoleArn key; its private contents are hidden here.
steps.note: There is no Copy button on this recorded AWS screen. The masked area is the real Value cell; keyboard copying is the instruction for your own screen.

steps.title: 7. Return to CryoStack and paste the full value into Role ARN.
instructions: Return to CryoStack and paste the full value into Role ARN.
The Role ARN field is filled; its contents are hidden in this guide.
Choose Verify connection and wait for the check.
Verifying changes to Connected when verification succeeds.
Confirm Connected and check Last verified.
Connected, Temporary role and an updated Last verified time.
steps.why: This selects the role CryoStack will use for temporary AWS access. CryoStack tests access through the newly created role. This confirms access through the role you just created.
steps.expected: Connected, Temporary role and an updated Last verified time.

steps.title: Next. Continue with cloud preparation and your model tutorial.
instructions: This first-time guide created the access-role stack and verified the new connection.
Continue to the model’s cloud preparation and readiness steps. Configure MATLAB only for a workflow that needs it.
BYO jobs bill the connected AWS account. Read Review & Launch and its estimate before submitting a paid run.
steps.why: A verified account is the starting point for readiness checks and paid cloud runs.
steps.expected: Check the connected account, resources and launch estimate before submitting a job.
steps.note: Silent recording; login and waiting time are omitted. Account identifiers, full role ARNs, template query and connection security values are masked. No cloud preparation or model job was submitted in this connection guide.
